title: Bridgehead intake and pinstamp for open weights
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Problem: The current model intake pipeline has brittle heuristics for community checkpoints (naming, sharded manifests, mixed quantized formats) and a non-cryptographic pinflow that leads to ambiguous artifact identity across conversions. This causes repeatable production surprises when a variant mismatch slips into a runtime pin.

Objective: Build a resilient "bridgehead" intake workflow that accepts arbitrary OSS weights archives, performs deterministic conversion into our canonical runtime format, runs a compact but representative smoke validation, and produces a cryptographically verifiable pinstamp (artifact ID + signed manifest) that can be consumed by the profile publisher and deployment pipelines.

Scope: 
- Ingest: rate-limited uploader + manifest extractor for mixed archives (tar/zip/hf-zip shards).
- Normalize: deterministic layer ordering, dtype normalization, and optional quantization metadata capture (no auto-quantization in this ticket).
- Convert: export to runtime-optimized format with stable ordering and metadata embedding.
- Validate: run micro-bench smoke (latency, sample fidelity, KV cache sanity) and safety checks (shape/precision assertions).
- Pinstamp: compute content-addressable hash, sign with key-rotation-aware signer, and emit a signed manifest and pin identifier for downstream publishing.
- Publish: push profile metadata to the catalog (separate ticket) but emit the profile-ready payload here.
acceptance_criteria: Bridgehead can accept demos of mixed-format community checkpoints (tar + .safetensors + shards) without manual pre-processing.
Conversion output is byte-for-byte deterministic for identical inputs and deterministic across repeated runs in CI (modulo kafka timestamps), reproducible via a --repro flag.
Pinstamp includes: content-address hash (sha256), conversion provenance (tool version + args), and a signer signature; the signed manifest verifies locally with the published verification key.
Smoke validation runs in < 120s for 7B-class models and returns a small structured report (latency P50/P95, sample output checksum, kv-cache-check true/false).
Artifacts (converted weights + signed manifest) are staged in the artifact-bucket under a predictable path and accessible to the Profile Publisher pipeline.
Automated tests (unit + integration) cover manifest parsing, signature verification, and determinism checks and are added to CI with flakiness < 1% over 50 runs.
Telemetry events emitted for key steps (ingest/convert/validate/pin) with correlation id and telemetry schema v2.
design_notes: Use a two-stage ingest: (1) lightweight scanner extracts file list and heuristics (safetensors vs torch), (2) sandboxed converter in ephemeral container handles heavy ops.

Deterministic conversion: sort tensors by stable key (module path), zero-pad names consistently, strip non-deterministic metadata fields, and normalize float dtypes to a canonical representation for the runtime.

Pinstamp algorithm: compute sha256 over canonical serialized representation (header + sorted tensor blobs), append conversion metadata, then sign with redwood-pins key managed via KMS; support key rotation by including key-id in manifest.

Safety checks: verify layer dimension continuity, detect missing attention weights, and run a small prompt through an isolated runner to assert that top-1 tokens are producible (checksum approach) rather than semantic judgment.
Sandboxing: conversion runs in gVisor container with strict tmpfs limits; network disabled except to read artifacts from the artifact-store and to write the final manifest to the staging bucket.
Fallbacks: if conversion fails due to unsupported ops, emit a clear failure artifact and a ticketable diagnostic bundle for manual triage; do not surface a false pinstamp.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable bridgehead for internal model ingestion only; restrict to team members and tag builds with 'canary-bridgehead'.
Phase 2 (partner): open to selected community uploaders and monitor failures and validation metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (general): enable for all OSS intake and wire into profile publisher; monitor for 7 days before flip to default in production.
Rollback: if >3% of ingests fail deterministically or if signed manifests cannot be verified by downstream services, revert to previous ingest path and disable automated publishing.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical serialization and sha256 calculation (edge cases for non-ASCII tensor names).
Integration test in CI cluster running conversion for 3 sample checkpoints (2.7B, 7B, 13B) validating determinism and smoke metrics stability.
Fuzz harness for input archive layouts (sharded naming permutations) to validate extractor robustness.
Manual end-to-end run: human-approved ingestion of a community checkpoint with cross-check by a PM and a runtime engineer.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Conversion non-determinism due to library versions. Mitigation: pin converter's runtime container image and include converter git sha in manifest.
Risk: Key compromise. Mitigation: use KMS-backed keys with rotation policy; include key-id and signature timestamp in manifest for revocation checks.
Risk: High latency for large checkpoints. Mitigation: incremental chunked conversion and ability to run a fast metadata-only smoke to gate publishing.
Risk: False positives in smoke validation (overfitting to micro-prompts). Mitigation: maintain a small prompt set covering tokenizer edge cases and length distributions.
decisions: We will NOT perform on-the-fly quantization in this ticket; quantization workflows live in Optimize.
Signed manifest will use SHA-256 as canonical hash and KMS-based signing with explicit key-id metadata.
Conversion will emit both runtime-optimized binaries and a lightweight index for quick KV-cache warming by the runtime.

2025-02-22 Rahul Singh (review): Left feedback on signer integration—need to include key-id and timestamp in manifest for rotation. Also flagged signing latency; suggested batching signature computations off the critical path.
2025-02-25 Emily Chen: Implemented key-id in manifest and moved signature generation to a post-conversion async step; conversion latency now within target. Added unit tests for sha256 edge cases.
